BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
BENENTR212.contribution: Examines organisational strategy and responsible digital transformation.
BENENTR212.evidence: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.

findings: The first plan studies public governance through comparative institutions, public law, EU politics, sustainability governance and public economics. Public Policy Analysis replaces Peace & Conflict to develop direct policymaking and policy-writing experience. Its description supports a policy-memo exercise and a concrete policy case. Constitutional law supports administrative constraints and remedies within a comparative approach; public international law and EU politics broaden the institutions lens. History supplies an independent research paper in a different field. Methods & Statistics and Qualitative Research Methodology provide relevant tools for public research. Utrecht has a deeper sequence in Dutch administration, public-service management and year-by-year organisation-based research culminating in a required thesis.

The second plan focuses on leadership and organisational practice through introductory business and personal leadership, leadership communication, organisational psychology, leading under pressure, digital strategy and negotiation. Comparative politics, constitutional law, public economics and sociology retain a public-purpose anchor. Cross-border business governance and commercial law serve as organisational context. Style & Meaning adds close language analysis. Peace & Conflict applies institutional analysis to reconciliation. The business and leadership material does not replicate Dutch public-service management or its required professional and field-research sequence.

Both 24-course plans fit current offerings and prerequisites. The governance plan uses introductory economics in term one and separates the policy course from its earlier comparative politics foundation. The organisation plan places leading under pressure before advanced organisational psychology. Both place sociology before qualitative methods and statistics before courses requiring it. Public Economics and Negotiation run in term four in both plans, and Transnational Business Law in term four in the organisation plan. A third direction lacks a separate source-backed generator. Academic disposition remains unresolved pending external formal requirements.
